title: Corrosion and simple cells
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank card covers galvanic cells at a deeper level (standard electrode potentials, cell voltage calculations, salt bridge) and does not cover rusting or corrosion, so it is related but not the same point as the brief.

draft.title: Corrosion and simple cells
card: the slow breakdown of a metal by reaction with its surroundings. Rusting is the corrosion of iron, and it is a redox reaction.
iron is oxidised: Fe → Fe²⁺ + 2e-. Oxygen is reduced. Water must be present, and salt in the water speeds the process up. The iron ions go on to form hydrated iron oxide, or rust.
a set-up where redox turns chemical energy into electrical energy. The two half-reactions happen at separate electrodes, and electrons travel along an external wire.
Oxidation happens at the anode and reduction at the cathode. Electrons flow from the anode to the cathode through the wire. A primary cell cannot be recharged.
draft.remember: Rusting and cells are both redox. In a cell, electrons flow from the anode to the cathode.

a.q: What happens to iron when it rusts?
opts: It is oxidised, losing electrons to form iron ions
It is reduced, gaining electrons to form iron ions
It is oxidised, gaining electrons from oxygen
It is reduced, losing electrons to oxygen
a.why: Iron atoms lose electrons to become iron ions, which is oxidation. Oxygen gains those electrons and is the species reduced. Saying iron is reduced mixes up the direction of electron transfer.

b.q: In a simple cell, a zinc electrode is oxidised and a copper electrode is where reduction occurs. Which describes the electron flow in the external wire?
opts: From the zinc anode to the copper cathode
From the copper cathode to the zinc anode
From the zinc cathode to the copper anode
From the copper anode to the zinc cathode
b.why: Oxidation happens at the anode, so zinc is the anode and releases electrons. Electrons flow through the wire to the cathode, where reduction occurs. That is the copper electrode, so the flow is from zinc to copper.
b.clue: Oxidation happens at the anode, and electrons flow away from it.

a.best: It is oxidised, losing electrons to form iron ions

b.best: From the zinc anode to the copper cathode
